images.title: Taking odd numbers from 38 leaves 2
images.purpose: Shows 38 as a bar cut into pieces of 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and 11 with 2 left over, so 38 is not a perfect square.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One long horizontal bar across the centre, divided into seven pieces, with its total above.
images.exact_structure: One horizontal bar of total length 38 units, divided into exactly 7 pieces whose widths are in proportion to their numbers. From left to right: pieces of 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and 11, filled alternately teal (#0072B2) and amber (#E69F00) starting with teal, each labelled with its number inside or just under it; then a last piece of width 2 filled vermilion (#D55E00) and labelled 2 left. A brace above the whole bar is labelled 38. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A number is a perfect square only if taking away 1, 3, 5 and so on lands exactly on 0.
images.description: Shows 38 as a bar cut into pieces of 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 and 11 with 2 left over, so 38 is not a perfect square.
images.context: 38 = 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 9 + 11 + 2; the next odd number, 13, is too big.

image_decisions.why: A bar cut into odd pieces with a leftover shows directly why 38 misses being a square.
